card.title: Second Place Feels Like Disappearing
card.instruction: Treat every comparison as a threat to your worth. Respond by proving that you still matter before the moment can move on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before announcing first place, could you say my name again with 'second'?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use my name in that sentence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Keep looking this way while they fetch the bigger trophy.

mechanism: A treats second-place comparison as threatened visibility and repeatedly demands personal acknowledgment.
confusable: Unlike ordinary pride, A must prevent attention moving to the better result by proving their own presence matters.
comparison: S207-a manages an announcer's words and gaze; S207-b places themself beside a photograph to capture attention.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
